Digital exhibition · First cycle 2026 · Testimony & Family Memory

“Що е човек?” — “What Is a Human?”

A visual history of one family story from Senokos, near the Serbia–Bulgaria border, places testimony, drawings and landscape together to ask what it means to live with poverty, movement and historical change.

Kremena DimitrovaIllustrated visual historyWho Owns Memory? · 2026

Encounter the story

History through places, objects and voices

The graphic history follows testimony and family memory across the Serbia–Bulgaria border region, asking how poverty, migration and care are carried across generations.

The chapters below bring the contributor’s sources and images into a readable, illustrated public-history narrative. Photographs and visual records can be enlarged by selecting them.

Central public-history question
What can one life tell us about the memory of poverty and migration across generations?
The original work

See the project’s visual language

This is an original visual from the participant’s submitted work. It provides a point of entry to the project’s historical argument and digital form.

Chapter 01

A life across a divided borderland

This illustrated graphic history follows memories associated with a family story in the Serbia–Bulgaria border region.

Chapter 02

What remains in testimony

The work combines recorded conversation, illustrations, historical images and maps to examine poverty, labour, care and migration across generations.

Chapter 03

A graphic form for public history

Instead of presenting a single authoritative account, the pages juxtapose the subject’s voice with wider borderland histories and the contemporary experiences of refugees.
